subject: Problem with subsamples of a multiple group analysis: not converged and negative covariance

messages.author: 1791d59ad7556b60
messages.subject: Problem with subsamples of a multiple group analysis: not converged and negative covariance
parts:
I am analyzing data with a multiple group SEM model which looks like this:

> sem.model_2 <- '
+   # measurement model
+   SES =~ 1*isei08 + eduyrs + hinctnta
+   ATTITUDE =~ 1*imtcjob + imbleco + imwbcrm
+   ALLOW =~ allow
+ 
+   # structural model
+   ATTITUDE ~ SES
+   ALLOW ~ SES + ATTITUDE
+ 
+   # residual correlations
+   imbleco ~~  imwbcrm
+   imtcjob ~~  imwbcrm
+ '

The model seems to be fine, but I suspect that the structure may be different for people with different income, so I am trying to fit the model using only sub-samples of people from high, middle or low income group; then two of groups (middle and low) got this warning:

(middle)
Warning message:
In lavaan::lavaan(model = sem.model_5, data = ESS7_use[ESS7_use$income_group ==  :
  lavaan WARNING: model has NOT converged!

With the verbose option, the output says the problem is singular convergence:

convergence status (0=ok):  1 
nlminb message says:  singular convergence (7) 
number of iterations:  1350 
number of function evaluations [objective, gradient]:  1754 1351

(low)
Warning messages:
1: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite;in group2. use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.
3: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite;in group3. use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.
And these are the covariance matrices

> inspect(fit_low, "cov.lv")[c(2,3)]
$`Group 2`
         SES    ATTITU ALLOW 
SES      -0.052              
ATTITUDE  3.892  3.457       
ALLOW     2.224  0.778  0.804

$`Group 3`
         SES   ATTITU ALLOW
SES      9.263             
ATTITUDE 5.392 3.145       
ALLOW    2.293 0.759  0.850


And the regression coefficients definitely doesn't look right.

My professor suggested me to use the result from the full sample as the starting value, and then drop one decile at a time to try to get a better starting value each time, but that still gets me either non-convergence or negative covariance at some point.

My initial suspicion was that it is because income decile (variable: hinctnta) is in the model and I am partitioning my sample with the same variable, but dropping it from the model didn't help.

Is there anything else I can try to solve these problems? Thanks a lot for any input!


My R script file and the data file are attached.

That would surprise me.  The ATTITUDE construct only has 3 indicators, so it is just identified.  There isn't any leftover information to estimate 2 of 3 possible residual correlations among the indicators.

messages.subject: Re: Problem with subsamples of a multiple group analysis: not converged and negative covariance
parts: Thanks for pointing this out! I dropped the second residual correlation and now the model converge with no problem using the subsamples.
Your construct still is not identified unless you drop all residual correlations, or impose equality constraints on the factor loadings.  Count your parameters and sample moments.
But then I don't understand why was it able to converge using the full sample? I always thought that if the model can converge then it means there is no identification problem.

Not necessarily.  Identification rules are largely heuristic and difficult to program checks for (see some recent heated discussion on this topic in the April SEMNET archives, centered around Judea Pearl challenging conventional wisdom).  Sometimes an optimization algorithm can find a local maximum and stop searching, thinking it found a unique solution.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
